en: 50 g white rice
50 g shredded chicken breast
5 cups water or stock
Ginger slices, spring onion
1 tsp soy sauce, sesame oil
Rinse the rice and put it in the pot with water and ginger
Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 minutes, stirring often
Add the chicken for the last 10 minutes
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil, top with spring onion
2 eggs
150 ml warm water or stock
1 tsp soy sauce
Half tsp sesame oil
Chopped spring onion, a pinch of salt
Beat the eggs with the warm water and salt
Strain the mixture through a sieve for a silky texture
Cover the bowl with foil and steam 12 minutes
Finish with soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onion

name.en: Soy milk with crisp bread strips

en: 1 cup unsweetened soy milk
2 slices wholegrain bread, cut into strips
Half tsp oil
A pinch of sugar or honey (optional)
Sesame seeds to garnish
Warm the soy milk on low heat without boiling
Brush the bread strips with oil and sprinkle sesame
Toast them in the oven or a dry pan until crisp
Serve the warm soy milk with the strips for dipping
Lean minced pork or turkey 100 g
Chopped spring onion and grated ginger
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp and a dash of sesame oil
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Sesame seeds for garnish
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the minced meat with the spring onion, ginger, soy sauce and sesame oil until combined.
Divide the dough into 4 small balls, roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each circle, gather the edges and seal tightly into a small pouch.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds, and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked and golden on the bottom.
Grated cabbage, grated carrot and chopped mushroom, 150 g total
Chopped spring onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp and a dash of sesame oil
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 90 g
A pinch of baking powder (if the dough doesn't already contain it)
Small parchment squares for steaming
Sauté the mushroom, cabbage and carrot with the spring onion and garlic in a dry pan for 4-5 minutes until softened and they lose their moisture.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and stir, let the filling cool.
Divide the dough into 3 balls, roll into circles, place the filling in the centre and gather the edges into pleats to form a sealed pouch.
Place each baozi on a parchment square, let rest 15 minutes, then steam for 12-15 minutes until puffed and fully cooked.
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
Water about 80 ml
1 egg
Chopped spring onion and chopped fresh coriander
Low-sodium sweet soy sauce 1 tsp
1 small crispy cracker or thin crisp for the filling (optional) and 1 tsp oil
Mix the flour with the water gradually until a smooth, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour in a thin layer of batter and spread evenly.
Crack the egg over the layer while still soft, spread it with a spoon, cook 1-2 minutes until set.
Flip the crepe, sprinkle with soy sauce, spring onion and coriander, add the cracker if desired, fold the edges inward and cut to serve immediately.

name.en: Baked Char Siu Bao (Sweet BBQ Pork Buns)

en: Cooked, shredded pork or turkey 80 g
Low-sodium sweet soy sauce 2 tbsp
1 small chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Cornflour half a tsp and a little water
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 90 g
A pinch of baking powder (if the dough doesn't already contain it)
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan for two minutes.
Add the shredded meat and soy sauce and stir for 3 minutes.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little water and add it, cook a minute until the sweet filling thickens, let it cool.
Divide the dough into 3 balls, roll into circles, stuff and seal with pleats, let rest 15 minutes, then steam 12-15 minutes until puffed and cooked.
White turnip, grated, 200 g
Rice flour 60 g and cornflour 1 tbsp
Lean turkey ham, small cubes, 30 g
Chopped spring onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp, a little salt and a pinch of white pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Boil the grated turnip in a little water for 5 minutes until softened, drain and reserve a little of the cooking water.
Mix the rice flour and cornflour with the cooking water gradually until a thick batter forms.
Add the turnip, ham, spring onion, garlic, soy sauce, salt and white pepper, mix well.

Pour the batter into a small greased tin, steam for 30-35 minutes until set, let cool completely, cut into slices and brown in an oven at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Cooked whole-wheat noodles 100 g
Spring onion, cut into long strips, 50 g
2 tbsp oil
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and 1 tsp dark soy sauce (optional)
A pinch of brown sugar
1 boiled egg to serve (optional)
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-low heat, add the spring onion and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until wilted, lightly toasted and the oil becomes fragrant.
Remove the toasted spring onion (you can keep it for garnish or discard it).
Add the light and dark soy sauce and brown sugar to the fragrant oil and stir.
Pour the oil over the cooked noodles and toss well, serve with the boiled egg if desired.

name.en: Steamed Rice Rolls (Cheung Fun) with Light Soy

en: Rice flour 60 g and cornflour 1 tbsp
Water about 150 ml and a pinch of salt
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp to serve
Water 1 tbsp and brown sugar half a tsp for the serving sauce
Chopped spring onion for garnish
A dash of sesame oil
Mix the rice flour and cornflour with the water and salt gradually until a smooth, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Grease a flat heatproof plate with a little oil, pour in a thin layer of batter.
Steam over high heat 3-4 minutes until it turns translucent and fully sets, remove and gently roll into a cylinder.
Mix the soy sauce, water and brown sugar for the serving sauce, pour it over the rolls, sprinkle with spring onion and sesame oil, and serve warm.
150 g chicken breast, sliced
100 g cooked rice
Broccoli, bell pepper, carrot
2 tbsp soy sauce, garlic, ginger
1 tsp oil, 1 tsp cornstarch
Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce, 10 minutes
Heat the oil on high and sear the chicken 4 minutes
Add garlic and ginger, then the vegetables, stir 3 minutes
Add the rest of the soy sauce and 2 tbsp water, serve with rice
100 g lean beef
80 g wheat noodles
3 cups beef stock
Pak choi, spring onion, ginger
2 tbsp soy sauce, cinnamon, star anise
Simmer the beef in the stock with ginger and spices 40 minutes
Add the soy sauce and simmer 10 minutes more
Boil the noodles separately and drain
Assemble noodles, broth and beef, add the pak choi
150 g chicken breast, cubed
Red and green bell pepper
10 g roasted peanuts
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar
Garlic, ginger, dried chilli
Sear the chicken in a hot pan 5 minutes and set aside
Sauté the garlic, ginger and dried chilli
Add the bell pepper, chicken, soy sauce and vinegar
Toss on high heat 2 minutes and add the peanuts
Cooked, chilled white rice 150 g
1 egg
Small peeled shrimp or diced chicken breast 50 g
Lean turkey ham, cubed, 30 g
Peas and carrot, small cubes, 60 g total
Chopped spring onion, low-sodium soy sauce 1 tsp and 1 tsp oil
Beat the egg, heat half the oil and scramble it quickly, chop into small pieces and set aside.
Add the remaining oil and cook the shrimp or chicken until done, add the ham, peas and carrot and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the chilled rice, breaking up clumps with the spatula, stir-fry over medium-high heat 4-5 minutes until heated through and well separated.
Add the chopped egg, soy sauce and spring onion, stir a final minute and serve hot.
Cooked whole-wheat noodles 100 g
Lean minced beef or chicken 70 g
Tahini or peanut butter 1 tbsp
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
1 crushed garlic clove, grated ginger and mild chili (optional)
Chopped spring onion and light vegetable stock 150 ml
Brown the minced meat in a dry pan for 5-6 minutes until fully cooked and lightly toasted.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute.
Mix the tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar and stock in a small bowl until combined.
Place the cooked noodles in a serving bowl, pour the tahini sauce over them, add the browned meat, sprinkle with spring onion and chili if desired, and serve hot.
Cooked whole-wheat noodles 100 g
Chicken breast, sliced, 90 g
Shredded cabbage, grated carrot and bell pepper, 100 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and chopped spring onion
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
1 tsp oil
Heat the oil and brown the garlic for a minute.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour and is nearly cooked.
Add the cabbage, carrot and bell pepper and stir for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and rice vinegar, stir well 2-3 minutes until combined and heated through, garnish with spring onion and serve hot.
Lean minced chicken or turkey 100 g
1 crushed garlic clove, grated ginger and chopped spring onion
Low-sodium soy sauce half a tsp and a dash of sesame oil
Wonton wrappers or very thin pastry, 8 pieces (60 g)
Light vegetable stock 500 ml
Chopped spinach or bok choy 50 g to serve
Mix the minced meat with the garlic, ginger, spring onion, soy sauce and sesame oil until combined.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wonton wrapper, fold into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Bring the stock to a boil in a pot, add the spinach or bok choy and cook for two minutes.
Add the wontons and simmer 5-6 minutes until they float and are fully cooked, and serve hot.
Cooked, chilled whole-wheat noodles 100 g
Tahini or peanut butter 2 tbsp
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
Warm water 30 ml to thin the sauce
1 crushed garlic clove and mild chili (optional)
Grated cucumber 50 g and chopped spring onion for garnish
Mix the tahini with the soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic and warm water gradually until you get a smooth, pourable sauce.
Place the chilled noodles in a serving bowl.
Pour the sauce over them and toss well until evenly coated.
Garnish with the grated cucumber, spring onion and chili if desired, and serve cold.
Firm tofu, cut into strips, 80 g
Sliced mushroom and grated carrot, 80 g total
1 egg
Rice vinegar 2 tbsp and low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp
A pinch of ground white pepper and mild chili (optional)
Cornflour 1 tsp and light vegetable stock 500 ml
Bring the stock to a boil in a pot, add the mushroom and carrot and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tofu, soy sauce, rice vinegar, white pepper and chili if desired.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little water and add it, cook 2 minutes until the texture thickens slightly.
Beat the egg and pour it slowly in a swirl while stirring constantly to form threads, cook a final minute and serve hot.
White rice 150 g and water 250 ml
Chicken breast, small cubes, 100 g
Sliced shiitake mushroom 50 g
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and a dash of sesame oil
Grated ginger and 1 crushed garlic clove
Chopped spring onion for garnish
Wash the rice and place it with the water in a thick-bottomed pot, cook over medium heat until the water starts to dry up.
Mix the chicken with the ginger, garlic and a spoonful of soy sauce, let it sit 10 minutes.
Arrange the marinated chicken and mushroom over the nearly-dry rice, cover and reduce the heat to minimum, cook 15-18 minutes without lifting the lid until the chicken and rice are fully cooked.
Drizzle the remaining soy sauce and sesame oil over it, garnish with spring onion and serve hot directly from the pot.
200 g soft tofu, cubed
70 g lean minced meat
1 tbsp spicy bean paste
Garlic, ginger, spring onion
1 tsp cornstarch, Sichuan pepper
Blanch the tofu a minute in salted water and drain
Brown the meat, then add garlic, ginger and the paste
Add half a cup of water and slide in the tofu gently
Stir in the dissolved cornstarch until the sauce thickens
170 g white fish fillet
A piece of ginger, finely sliced
3 spring onions
2 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tsp sesame oil, coriander
Lay half the ginger and onion under the fish on a plate
Steam 8-10 minutes until the flesh flakes
Discard the pooled liquid and top with fresh ginger
Heat the oil until smoking, pour it over, then the soy sauce
150 g lean beef, sliced
1 tbsp fermented black beans
Broccoli and bell pepper
1 garlic clove, ginger
1 tsp cornstarch, soy sauce
Toss the beef with the cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce, 10 minutes
Mash the black beans with the garlic and ginger
Sear the beef on high heat 3 minutes and set aside
Sauté the vegetables and black beans, return the beef for 2 minutes

name.en: Baked Sweet and Sour Chicken with Rice

en: Chicken breast, cubed, 140 g
Red bell pepper and pineapple, cubed, 100 g total
1 onion, cut into small squares
Rice vinegar 2 tbsp and low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp
Pineapple or orange juice 2 tbsp and brown sugar 1 tsp
Cornflour 1 tsp and 1 tsp oil
Marinate the chicken in a little soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Arrange the chicken, pepper, onion and pineapple on a lined tray, brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until the chicken is fully cooked.

Mix the rice vinegar, remaining soy sauce, pineapple juice, brown sugar and dissolved cornflour in a small pot, cook 3-4 minutes until it thickens, pour over the chicken and vegetables and serve with the rice.

name.en: Braised Eggplant in Garlic Sauce with Rice

en: Eggplant, cut into sticks, 300 g
3 crushed garlic cloves and grated ginger
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
Spicy bean paste or light tomato sauce 1 tsp (optional)
Cornflour half a tsp and light vegetable stock 100 ml
Chopped spring onion, 1 tsp oil and cooked basmati rice 110 g
Heat the oil and brown the garlic and ginger for a minute.
Add the eggplant and stir for 5-6 minutes until it starts to soften.
Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar, spicy bean paste and stock, cover and cook over medium heat 8-10 minutes until the eggplant is fully cooked.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little water and add it, cook 2 minutes until it thickens, garnish with spring onion and serve with the rice.
Chicken breast, cubed, 140 g
Fresh orange juice 60 ml and grated orange zest
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
1 crushed garlic clove and grated ginger
Brown sugar half a tsp and cornflour half a tsp
Chopped spring onion for garnish and 1 tsp oil
Arrange the chicken on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked.
Mix the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, brown sugar and cornflour in a small pot, cook over medium heat 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Pour the sauce over the baked chicken and toss, garnish with spring onion and serve with the rice.

name.en: Steamed Chicken with Ginger and Scallion with Rice

en: Skinless chicken breast or thighs 140 g
Ginger, thinly sliced, and spring onion, cut into long strips
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar half a tsp
Sesame oil 1 tsp and a little salt
1 crushed garlic clove
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Place the chicken in a heatproof dish, arrange the ginger slices and garlic over it.
Steam for 18-20 minutes until fully cooked.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil and salt.
Remove the chicken, pour the sauce over it and arrange the spring onion, and serve with the rice.
Chicken breast, cubed, 140 g
Raw cashews 25 g
Red and green bell pepper and onion, cut into squares, 100 g total
Low-sodium soy sauce 2 tbsp and rice vinegar 1 tsp
1 crushed garlic clove and grated ginger
Cornflour half a tsp and 1 tsp oil
Toast the raw cashews in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes until golden, set aside.
Heat the oil and brown the garlic and ginger for a minute.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour, add the peppers and onion and stir for 4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar and dissolved cornflour, cook 2 minutes until the sauce thickens, add the toasted cashews and stir, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Steamed Tofu with Minced Pork and Soy with Rice

en: Soft tofu 200 g
Lean minced chicken or pork 70 g
1 crushed garlic clove and grated ginger
Low-sodium soy sauce 1 tbsp and rice vinegar half a tsp
A dash of sesame oil and chopped spring onion for garnish
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Place the tofu in a heatproof dish.
Brown the minced meat with the garlic and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes until fully cooked.
Add the soy sauce and rice vinegar to the meat and stir.
Spread the meat over the tofu, steam for 10-12 minutes until the tofu is heated through, drizzle with sesame oil and spring onion, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Salt and Pepper Shrimp with Rice

en: Peeled medium shrimp 160 g
Cornflour 2 tbsp
2 crushed garlic cloves and finely chopped hot green chili (optional)
A little salt and coarsely ground black pepper
Chopped spring onion for garnish and 2 tsp oil
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Dry the shrimp thoroughly with a paper towel, coat in the cornflour until fully covered.
Arrange on a lined tray with space between them, brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Brown the garlic and green chili in a dry pan for a minute, add the baked shrimp, salt and black pepper and toss quickly, garnish with spring onion and serve with the rice.
100 g soy bean pods
2 garlic cloves, chopped
Half tsp sesame oil
1 tsp soy sauce
A pinch of chilli, salt
Boil the pods 5 minutes in salted water
Heat the sesame oil and soften the garlic without burning
Add the pods, soy sauce and chilli, toss 2 minutes
Serve warm or chilled
2 cucumbers
2 garlic cloves, crushed
1 tsp rice vinegar
1 tsp sesame oil and soy sauce
Toasted sesame, a pinch of sugar, salt
Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife, then cut into chunks
Salt them, wait 10 minutes and drain the water
Mix the garlic, vinegar, oil, soy sauce and sugar
Pour over the dressing, sprinkle sesame and serve cold
100 g firm tofu, cubed
Half tsp five-spice powder
1 tsp cornstarch
1 tsp oil
Soy sauce to serve
Pat the tofu cubes dry with a towel
Toss with the cornstarch and spice, gently
Pan-fry in the oil 8 minutes, turning, until crisp
Serve hot with soy sauce for dipping
Grated cabbage, grated carrot and chopped mushroom, 150 g total
Chopped spring onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Low-sodium soy sauce half a tsp and a dash of sesame oil
Spring roll wrappers or thin pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
Egg white for brushing
1 tsp oil
Brown the cabbage, carrot and mushroom with the spring onion and garlic in a dry pan for 4-5 minutes until softened and they lose their moisture.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and stir, let the filling cool slightly.
Place a spoonful of filling on each pastry sheet, roll tightly into a thin cylinder, seal the edge with egg white.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 35 ml and a pinch of salt
Finely chopped spring onion 30 g
Sesame oil 1 tsp for the dough
1 tsp oil for brushing
A little extra salt for sprinkling
Knead the flour with the warm water and salt gradually until a soft dough forms, let it rest 15 minutes.
Roll it out on a lightly floured surface into a thin rectangle, brush with sesame oil and sprinkle with the spring onion and salt.
Roll it up tightly from the long edge into a cylinder, then coil it into a spiral and gently flatten again into a disc.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Lean minced chicken 80 g
Chopped spring onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Low-sodium soy sauce half a tsp and a dash of sesame oil
Wonton wrappers, 8 pieces (50 g)
Egg white for brushing
1 tsp oil
Mix the minced chicken with the spring onion, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil until combined.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wonton wrapper, fold into a triangle and press the edges with egg white to seal tightly.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and fully crisp.
Glutinous rice flour 50 g
Boiled, mashed sweet potato 40 g
Brown sugar 2 tsp
Sesame seeds 25 g for coating
Low-sugar sweet red bean paste 2 tbsp for the filling (optional)
1 tsp oil for brushing
Knead the rice flour with the mashed sweet potato and brown sugar gradually until you get a soft, cohesive dough.
Shape into small balls, if desired press each ball to form a small hollow, fill with red bean paste and seal well.
Moisten the balls with a little water and roll in the sesame seeds until fully coated.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 190°C for 20-22 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Peeled shrimp, coarsely chopped, 120 g
Chopped spring onion and grated ginger
Cornflour half a tsp and a dash of sesame oil
A little salt and low-sodium soy sauce half a tsp
Wonton wrappers or thin pastry sheets, 5 pieces (50 g)
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the chopped shrimp with the spring onion, ginger, cornflour, sesame oil, salt and soy sauce until combined.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each pastry sheet, moisten the edges and seal with small pleats into a half-moon shape.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until the shrimp is fully cooked and the pastry turns golden.
Peeled shrimp, finely chopped, 80 g
1 egg white and chopped spring onion
Cornflour half a tsp and a dash of sesame oil
A little salt
Whole-wheat bread, 2 slices (60 g)
Sesame seeds 20 g for coating
Mix the chopped shrimp with the egg white, spring onion, cornflour, sesame oil and salt until a cohesive mixture forms.
Spread the mixture evenly over the bread slices, press gently.
Dip the covered side in the sesame seeds to coat fully.
Arrange on a lined tray with the sesame side up, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until the shrimp is cooked and the sesame is golden, cut into triangles and serve hot.
Cabbage, cut into large pieces, and carrot, cut into sticks, 200 g total
Rice vinegar 60 ml and water 60 ml
Brown sugar 1 tsp and salt half a tsp
A pinch of dried mild chili (optional)
1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch of Sichuan peppercorns (optional)
Ginger, thinly sliced
Mix the rice vinegar, water, brown sugar and salt in a bowl until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Add the garlic, Sichuan peppercorns, ginger and chili if desired.
Add the cabbage and carrot and toss until fully coated with the solution.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight before serving, the longer it sits the more flavourful it becomes.
50 g adzuki red beans
3 cups water
1 tsp sugar or honey
A piece of dried orange peel
A pinch of salt
Soak the beans overnight and drain them
Simmer in the water with the orange peel for an hour
Mash a third of the beans to make the soup creamy
Add the sugar and salt, simmer 5 more minutes
1 cup unsweetened almond milk
2 g agar powder
1 tsp honey
Half tsp almond extract
Fresh fruit to serve
Dissolve the agar in half a cup of water and boil 2 minutes
Add the almond milk and honey, heat without boiling
Stir in the almond extract and pour into a mould
Chill 2 hours, cut into cubes and serve with fruit
1 piece fresh ginger, peeled
2 cups water
2 tbsp light brown sugar or honey
A piece of orange peel (optional)
Cubed silken tofu (optional)
Crush or thinly slice the ginger
Boil it in the water with the orange peel for 15 minutes
Add the sugar or honey and stir until dissolved
Add the tofu if you like and serve warm

name.en: Light Mango Sago with Coconut Milk

en: Small sago (tapioca) pearls 30 g
Ripe mango, cubed, 100 g
Light coconut milk 80 ml
Low-fat milk 60 ml
Honey or brown sugar 1 tsp
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Boil the sago pearls in boiling water 10-12 minutes until translucent, drain and rinse with cold water.
Blend half the mango with the coconut milk, milk and honey until smooth.
Add the drained sago to the mixture and stir.
Pour into a serving bowl, garnish with the remaining mango cubes and mint if desired, and serve cold.
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (40 g)
1 egg
Low-fat milk 60 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp
Vanilla extract half a tsp
A pinch of salt
Line a small greased tart tin with the pastry, prick the base with a fork.
Beat the egg with the milk, brown sugar, vanilla and salt until the sugar fully dissolves.
Pour the mixture evenly over the pastry.
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until the filling sets and the pastry turns golden, let cool slightly before serving.

name.en: Light Ma Lai Go (Steamed Chinese Sponge Cake)

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g
2 eggs
Brown sugar 30 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
Baking powder half a tsp
1 tsp oil for the tin
Beat the eggs with the brown sugar using an electric whisk for 4-5 minutes until the mixture becomes pale and thick.
Add the milk and mix gently, then gradually fold in the flour and baking powder until combined without deflating the mixture.
Pour the batter into a small greased tin.
Steam over medium heat 18-20 minutes until fully cooked and it springs back when pressed gently, let cool slightly before slicing.
Toasted black sesame seeds 30 g
Cooked white rice 2 tbsp
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Brown sugar 20 g
A pinch of salt
About 50 ml water to thin the texture
Grind the toasted black sesame seeds in a grinder or strong blender until finely powdered.
Add the cooked rice and milk and blend until completely smooth.
Pour the mixture into a small pot, add the brown sugar, salt and water, cook over low heat 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until the texture thickens like a creamy soup.
Pour into a serving bowl and serve warm.
Small tapioca pearls 30 g
Light coconut milk 150 ml
Low-fat milk 60 ml
Brown sugar 20 g
A pinch of salt
1 egg
Soak the tapioca pearls in warm water for 30 minutes until slightly plump, drain.
Beat the egg with the coconut milk, milk, brown sugar and salt.
Add the soaked tapioca and mix.
Pour the mixture into a small oven-safe dish, bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until fully set, let cool slightly before serving.
Water 250 ml
Dried osmanthus flowers 1 tsp (or 1 osmanthus tea bag)
Honey 2 tbsp
Plant-based gelatin (agar agar) 1 tsp
A little lemon juice
Fresh fruit pieces for garnish (optional)
Boil the water in a small pot, add the osmanthus flowers or tea bag and let it steep 5 minutes, strain.
Return the infused water to the pot, add the plant-based gelatin and cook over low heat 2 minutes, stirring, until fully dissolved.
Remove from the heat, add the honey and lemon juice and stir.
Pour into serving cups, chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours until set, garnish with fresh fruit pieces if desired and serve cold.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Coarsely ground walnuts 30 g
Brown sugar 30 g
Vegetable oil 2 tbsp
A pinch of baking powder
A pinch of salt and small walnut pieces for garnish
Mix the flour, ground walnuts, brown sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Gradually add the oil and mix with your hands until a cohesive dough forms (add a little water if needed).
Shape into small balls, flatten each ball slightly with your hand, place a small walnut piece in the centre of each disc.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 180°C for 16-18 minutes until golden on the bottom, let cool completely before serving to become crisp.
